# Appeal of Denial – Neck (Cervical) Fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551

**RE: Request for Reconsideration of Adverse Benefit Determination**
Member: Jordan Alvarez
Member ID: W482428991
Reference Number: POC-177B09D7A6-51151
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-11

Dear UnitedHealthcare Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551, as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-11 (reference number POC-177B09D7A6-51151). This determination was made under the plan's policy **"Spinal Fusion and Decompression" (2026T0639I)** (https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/spinal-fusion-decompression.pdf), and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision in light of that same policy and the records my surgeon has submitted.

## Why I am appealing

The denial states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I do not believe this is consistent with either my medical records or the plan's own stated coverage rationale. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and the record shows the following:

- **MRI cervical spine, 2026-06-04:** C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression.
- **Exam findings:** positive provocative testing on the affected side, with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, and radicular pain, numbness, and weakness into the right thumb and index finger.
- **Symptom duration:** 24 months of progressive neck pain unrelieved by rest.
- **Conservative treatment already completed:** 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-05-14 through 2026-07-09) including cervical traction and postural training, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; 4 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-03 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

The plan's own policy states:

> "Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

and

> "Surgery may be an option for individuals whose pain cannot be controlled by more conservative methods (National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, 2023)."

My records show exactly this pattern: nearly two years of progressive pain, imaging confirming a specific structural cause (C5-C6 disc herniation with nerve root compression), a corresponding neurologic deficit on exam, and a documented course of conservative treatment — physical therapy, medication, and an injection — that did not resolve the problem. This is the situation the plan's own policy describes as one in which surgery "may be an option."

I also want to note that the policy excerpt addressing structural instability — measured by "the difference in translational alignment between lumbar vertebrae greater than or equal to 3 mm between views, as documented by flexion-extension radiographs or comparison of a supine and upright image" — refers specifically to the **lumbar** spine. My procedure is a **cervical** fusion at C5-C6. If this lumbar-specific measurement was applied to my cervical case, I ask that the plan clarify why, since it does not appear to be the correct criterion for this level of the spine.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

The policy states that "[f]or medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the... Procedures, Decompression +/- Fusion, Lumbar (Custom) - UHG... InterQual® criteria." Because InterQual is licensed software and not something I can access on my own, I am asking the plan to provide me, in writing and free of charge, **the specific InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination** — including confirmation of which subset (cervical or lumbar) was actually used to review my request. Federal appeal rules entitle me to this information, and I would like it included in the file for this appeal.

The policy also states that "[m]edical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage." I have provided the imaging report, physical therapy discharge note, and clinical exam findings summarized above, and I ask that they be reviewed against whichever specific criteria applied to my determination.

## What I am asking for

I am asking UnitedHealthcare to reverse this denial and approve coverage for CPT 22551 based on the medical necessity documented by my surgeon, or, at minimum, to identify in writing the specific criteria used to deny this request so that I and my surgeon can respond to them directly.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-07** (180 days from the date of the denial notice, per that notice). I am submitting it through member.uhc.com and to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I am also available by phone at the number on my member ID card.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Jordan Alvarez
Member ID: W482428991
Date: [DATE]
Phone: [PHONE NUMBER]
Email: [EMAIL ADDRESS]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
